newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to change phone numbers on October 18.
newsitem.headline: France to change phone numbers on October 18.

text.p: France will fall in step with international telephone standards on October 18 when it adopts a 10-digit system in line with other countries.
France Telecom, the operator of standard telephone services, has mounted a massive publicity campaign to prepare the French for the change, the first since 1985.
France Telecom said the new system would allow France to have 470 million different numbers -- enough to last until 2050.
The main change for people calling from abroad will be that France will be carved up into five regions instead of just two currently -- Paris and the rest of France.
Telephone numbers in the central urban region around Paris will have the prefix 01. From abroad, these numbers will remain unchanged and begin with the French international code 33, followed by 1.
Northwestern France, which includes the cities Lille and Le Havre, will have the prefix 02, or 2 from abroad.
The Northeast and its cities including Strasbourg, Reims and Nancy will get the prefix 03, or 3 from abroad.
The Southeast, Marseilles, Lyon, Nice, will get 04 or 4 from abroad and the Southwest will have numbers staring with 05, or 5 from abroad.
Mobile telephone numbers, regardless of the owner's address, will have 06 added to the existing eight numbers.
The old regional 16 prefix will be scrapped.
Toll free numbers will start with 0 800.
The access number for overseas calls from France will change to 00 from 19.
